contexts.text: The evil of penalty is said to be permitted for the sake of the amendment of the evil... Hitherto no one has known what permission is. That which is permitted is supposed to be done by Him who permits, because He permits it. But the fact is quite otherwise.
But they are not permitted to speak falsity...
As man is such, he has been permitted, and is also now permitted (to kill animals and eat their flesh).
This is why man is permitted to live in pleasures, and in cupidities rather (than to commit profanation). Therefore the Jews are permitted to immerse themselves in avarice...
Whether from the Lord's will, leave, or permission.
Man is then permitted to attribute the power to himself...
Not the least can be inflicted on man by evil Spirits which is not from permission...
The Lord provides some things from permission, some from admission, some from leave, some from good pleasure, and some from will. AC 2447:2.
Suppose that as the Lord permits evil. He is the cause of evil.
It is afterwards insinuated that the Lord permits; but that all evil is from diabolical Spirits.
(Thus) sacrifices were not commanded, but permitted.
Some things of permission are from the laws of order as to good.
Although it is predicated of God that He permits, it is not according to the idea which man has of permission; namely, that by permitting He concurs...

That these ancients had concubines... was from permission, for the sake of the representation... This was of permission, because they had no conjugial love... To such there could be permissions without injury to conjugial love...
The Lord permits that such things should influence man at first...
Not permitted by the Divine. Signified.
Therefore it was permitted that they should have such an opinion concerning the resurrection.
(Why Hamor, etc., were permitted to be killed.)
When any such thing is permitted by the Lord, it is done through the evil, and through the infernals...
Such (cruelties) are never permitted except to such...
Nothing is permitted, except to the end that something of good may come of it. AC 6574:end.
The Lord permits the infernals in the other life to lead the good into temptation... This is the means by which spiritual life is gifted...
(The Hells) are not permitted to bring forth any other evils than such as can be turned into good...
Many things commanded by Jehovah, in the internal sense do not signify that they are commanded, but that they are permitted.

How the case is with permission cannot be told in a few words, because it involves very many arcana. When the impious are damned, and tormented, the permission is not from the Lord as of one who is willing, but as of one who is not willing...

It is believed that evils are from the Divine, from the fact that the Divine permits, and does not take them away; and he who permits, and does not take away when he can, appears as if he wills it so... But the Divine permits, because He cannot inhibit and take away evils. Explained.

Things from will are nearest the Lord; those from good-pleasure are a little more remote from Him; those from leave are still more remote; and those from permission are most remote from Him, These are the degrees of the influx and reception of the Divine; but each degree contains innumerable things... as, for instance, in the case of those things which happen from permission... for when a man examines them closely... he becomes confounded by the innumerable arcana therein; and yet the arcana of permission are relatively few...
Permission because they insisted. Signified, Explained.
To leave man to do evil from his freedom, is called to permit. NJHD 272.
Therefore the Lord permits evil, not as one who is willing; but as one who is not able to resist it for the sake of the end, which is salvation.
On the Knowledge of this law depends the Knowledge of the laws of permission.
On account of this danger (of profanation) the Lord permits evils of life, and many heretical things of worship.
That the laws of permission are also laws of the Divine Providence. Chapter.
It is said that God permits a thing, which does not mean that He wills it; but that He cannot avert it, on account of the end, which is salvation.
Leading man away from evil, and to good... cannot be done without the permission of evil.
Some things shall now be enumerated which are of permission, and still are according to the laws of the Divine Providence... DP 249. SE 2713.
Why the Divine Providence permits the impious in heart to be raised to dignities and enriched with wealth. Explained.
(Why wars are permitted.)
It follows that... the permissions of dissensions and heresies are also according to the laws of the Divine Providence.
That evils are permitted for the sake of the end, which is salvation. General article. DP 281, Explained.
That the Divine Providence with the evil is the continual permission of evil, to the end that there may be a continual withdrawal from it. Explained. DP 296:13. DP 333.
Granted to him = that it was permitted; for all falsities of doctrine, like evils of life, take place from permission. References.
It is therefore among the laws of permission... that they should falsify truths in so far as they are in evils of life.
That from the permission of evil... it evidently appears that man has free will in spiritual things. General article.

Concerning permissions. The doctrine of permissions is an entire doctrine. He who does not understand permissions, or conclude concerning permissions, falls into things of doubt and denial concerning the Power of God Messiah over the universe... Without permission no one can be reformed; for opposites must be induced...
Concerning permissions: that every single thing tends to the good of the universe, or of all. Explained.
How permissions are represented by nature. (Explained.)

Concerning permissions. - The doctrine of permissions involves also this: that evil Spirits pretend to dominate over the evil... But the permission does not extend further than that the man... may become better...
They can do nothing except from the Lord's good-pleasure, leave, or permission, which are distinct...
That the permissions of evils from Spirits are represented by the remission of their endeavours. Explained.
That the perversion of order is the general cause of permissions. Explained.
If a Spirit purposes to give thanks, he cannot do so at all, except by manifest permission and leave...
That the permission, leave, good-pleasure, and will, of the Lord, are in all things which happen; but in application to the subjects. Explained.
They are thus bent to such things as the Lord concedes, and permits, so that not a whit comes forth from them which is not of leave, if not evil; or of permission, if evil.
That evil punishes itself; and concerning permission. SE 4275.
Thou permittest the woman Jezebel ().
From these things it is evident, that the laws of permission, which are many, proceed from the laws of Providence.
By leading, if he acknowledges the Divine Providence... by permitting, if he does not acknowledge it.
